name: Anthropic candidate AI guidance
citation: Anthropic, 'How to collaborate with Claude during our hiring process' (page title 'Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage'), anthropic.com, last updated 10 July 2025. https://www.anthropic.com/candidate-ai-guidance (URL still live and unchanged as of 21 November 2026).
evidence_tier: Primary company statement (official hiring policy page).
access_status: Fully read (full page text retrieved 21 November 2026). Cross-checked against Tristan Hume's Anthropic engineering post (21 January 2026), which links to this exact URL as 'general candidate guidance', and Felix Rieseberg's 'Hunger beats tenure', both also opened in full.
sponsor_and_incentive: Anthropic itself. Anthropic sells Claude, so the page doubles as product promotion: it encourages candidates to use Claude to prepare and refine, names Claude throughout (with 'or other AI tools' mentioned once), and invites other employers to 'adapt this framework'. The restrictive parts (no AI in take-homes or live interviews by default) cut against that commercial interest, which makes them more credible as genuine policy.
exact_quotes: Header: 'How to collaborate with Claude during our hiring process' / 'Last updated Jul 10, 2025'. Intro: 'At Anthropic, we use Claude every day, so we're looking for candidates who excel at collaborating with AI.' and 'Here's when and how to use Claude (or other AI tools) when applying to and interviewing with Anthropic.' Applying: 'Please create your first draft yourself, then use Claude to refine it. We want to see your real experience, but Claude can polish how you communicate about your work.' Take-home assessments: 'Complete these without Claude unless we indicate otherwise. We'd like to assess your unique skills and strengths. We'll be clear when AI is allowed (example: "You may use Claude for this coding challenge").' Preparing for interviews: 'Use Claude to research Anthropic, practice your answers, and prepare questions for us.' Live interviews: 'This is all you–no AI assistance unless we indicate otherwise. We're curious to see how you think through problems in real time. If you require any accommodations for your interviews, please let your recruiter know early in the process.' Table, not allowed: 'Using Claude to create experiences' and 'Using Claude during assessments (unless permitted) ... Having Claude write your code when we haven't explicitly allowed it'. Why section: 'We encourage you to use it for preparation and refinement, and we're excited to get to know you and see your thinking in action during assessments and interviews.' 'Be yourself. Use AI to refine your ideas, not replace them. We want to see your actual experience and how you think—not AI-generated responses.' 'Be transparent. ... We expect the same transparency from you in following this guidance.' Anthropic's own use: 'We use Claude to create job descriptions, develop interview questions, draft and refine candidate communications, analyze hiring metrics, transcribe interviews, and identify candidates to source. We don't use your data to train Claude or let Claude make hiring decisions.' Closing: 'We plan to regularly review and update this guidance to reflect evolving AI capabilities.' and 'If you are designing a hiring process. Feel free to adapt this framework for your organization.' Related (Hume, 21 Jan 2026, section 'Compatibility with AI assistance'): 'Anthropic's general candidate guidance asks candidates to complete take-homes without AI unless indicated otherwise. For this take-home, we explicitly indicate otherwise.' and 'Some colleagues suggested banning AI assistance. I didn't want to do this.' Related (Rieseberg, 27 Oct 2026): 'As a hiring manager at Anthropic, I stopped asking candidates to do them.' and 'I haven't quite gotten there yet — but I'm scanning resumes and portfolios for little prototypes that exhibit taste, empathy, and principled thinking.'
date_and_recency: Last updated 10 July 2025 per the page. No newer revision shown as of 21 November 2026, despite the stated plan to 'regularly review and update'. It predates Hume's post (January 2026, Claude Opus 4.5 era) and Rieseberg's post (October 2026) and has not been revised to reflect either.
key_claims: Anthropic wants candidates 'who excel at collaborating with AI'. Policy by stage: (1) Application and resume: AI allowed for refining a first draft the candidate wrote; using AI to invent experiences or write application answers is not allowed. (2) Take-home assessments: no AI by default; AI allowed only where Anthropic explicitly says so. (3) Interview preparation: AI use encouraged. (4) Live interviews: no AI by default ('This is all you'), unless Anthropic indicates otherwise. Exceptions: the 'unless we indicate otherwise' carve-outs for take-homes and live interviews, and accommodations requested through the recruiter. Candidates are expected to be transparent about their AI use. Anthropic discloses it uses Claude in its own hiring workflow but says Claude does not make hiring decisions and candidate data is not used for training. The rationale for the default ban is to assess 'your unique skills and strengths' and 'how you think through problems in real time'.
headline_figures: None. The only date is 'Last updated Jul 10, 2025'. No numbers on candidates, roles or outcomes.
sample_and_method: Not applicable. A policy statement, not a study. Applies to all roles ('Regardless of which role you're applying for').
what_is_measured: By default, unaided individual skill: 'your unique skills and strengths' in take-homes and 'how you think through problems in real time' in live interviews, i.e. solo problem-solving without AI. The intro's stated hiring goal, candidates 'who excel at collaborating with AI', is not what the default-banned assessment stages measure; that skill is only invited in the application and prep stages, or where a specific assessment opts in.
ai_policy_in_interview: Banned by default in take-homes and live interviews, with explicit per-assessment exceptions allowed ('unless we indicate otherwise'). Encouraged for preparation; permitted for refining application materials.
scope_and_status: Rolled out, company-wide, all roles. Live public policy since at least 10 July 2025.
validity_evidence: None. The page offers no criterion-validity data for unaided versus AI-assisted assessment.
relevance_to_angle: Complicates and sharpens Lee's angle. The official default is the opposite of 'assess how they work with a coding agent': take-homes and live interviews are AI-free unless an assessment opts in. Within the same company, practice has moved away from that default. Hume's performance take-home is an explicit opt-out ('For this take-home, we explicitly indicate otherwise') and Hume rejected colleagues' suggestion to ban AI, wanting candidates to distinguish themselves 'in a setting with AI—like they'd have on the job'. Hume also says Anthropic still uses a live question that Claude models beat 'because our other live questions aren't AI-resistant either'. Rieseberg, speaking for his own teams, has dropped the coding interview entirely and looks for 'taste, empathy, and principled thinking' in prototypes. So the tension: a company-wide policy (July 2025) built to measure solo convergent skill, an engineering lead who opted out of it, and a hiring manager who stopped testing that skill. Useful for the essay as evidence that even an AI lab's written policy lags its interviewers. Also supports 'basic fluency' and 'communication' indirectly: the page wants candidates' authentic thinking and communication, and AI is welcomed for preparation. Note that the 'unless we indicate otherwise' clause means the policy technically accommodates Hume's take-home; it is a default, not a ban.
limitations_stated: The page says it will be revised: 'We plan to regularly review and update this guidance to reflect evolving AI capabilities.' No other limitations stated.
counter_evidence: The policy is a default with an explicit exception mechanism, so it is not strictly in conflict with Hume's AI-permitted take-home; Hume himself cites it and invokes the exception. Rieseberg writes as a hiring manager about his own teams, not company policy, so his practice does not show the company policy has changed. Anthropic still appears to run AI-free live coding questions (per Hume, January 2026). The 'no AI' default is defensible on Anthropic's own stated grounds: seeing real-time thinking, which partly overlaps with Lee's 'design conversation' format.
verification_status: Policy text, date (10 July 2025), stage-by-stage rules, exceptions and Anthropic's own-use disclosure: checked against the primary page, opened in full 21 November 2026. Hume quotes and the link from his post to this URL: checked against anthropic.com/engineering/AI-resistant-technical-evaluations (published 21 January 2026), opened. Rieseberg quotes: checked against felixrieseberg.com/hunger-beats-tenure-advice-for-junior-engineers/, opened. Whether any newer internal policy supersedes the public page: not verifiable.
